turns.t: Doctor, I'll be quick, my parking runs out at half past. My left ear is blocked up and I can barely hear on that side.
Right, quick it is. How long has it felt blocked up?
About three weeks now. My husband says the telly is far too loud, and I've stopped hearing the kettle.
Ha, the kettle, that's a good test. Did it come on suddenly, or creep up on you?
Crept up. My hearing's worse every week, and I just can't be doing with it.
What does it feel like inside? Pressure, or water, or something else?
Like I'm underwater, all full and muffled. Do you use cotton buds, is that what you're going to ask?
You read my mind. Do you?
Every morning, yes. I know, I know, everybody tells me off for it.
I'm not telling you off. They tend to push the wax further in, that's all.
Sorry to interrupt, Doctor. Her repeat prescription list is up on the screen, if you want it.
Thanks, nurse. While we have it, what are you taking at the moment?
Just my blood pressure one and the stomach acid one. Nurse knows the names, I never remember.
It says amlodipine 5 mg once a day, and omeprazole 20 mg once a day.
That's them. The amlodipine's for my high blood pressure, and the omeprazole's for the reflux.
Do you take them at the same time every day? I'm always curious how people manage.
Amlodipine with breakfast, omeprazole half an hour before. I've an alarm on my phone.
Sensible. My own mother used to line hers up next to the kettle. Anyway, anything else in your notes I should ask about?
I get migraines now and then, but that's a separate matter. Can we get on, please?
Of course. From what you describe, it's most likely a plug of wax pressing on the eardrum.
Wax? That's all it is? I thought I was going deaf.
That's my first thought, yes. I'd like the nurse to syringe your ears and clear it out.
I can do that. We've a slot on Tuesday morning if that suits.
Tuesday's fine. Does it hurt, though? I'm not good with needles.
There's no needle, it's just warm water. It's a bit noisy, and over in a few minutes.
Fine. As long as it's quick.
Then come and see me after the syringing, next Tuesday, and I'll check how your hearing is doing.
So Tuesday for both. Can the same parking ticket cover it, do you know?
Ha, afraid not. But reception can give you a token for the machine.
Until then, leave the cotton buds alone, and keep water out of that ear.
Hard habit to break, but I'll try. I'll hide them from myself.
Put them at the back of the cupboard. Out of sight helps with most habits.
True. Right, I really must dash. Thank you both.
Go on, off you go before the meter runs out. See you Tuesday.
Bye, Doctor. Bye, nurse.
Mind how you go. Pop to reception on the way out for that token.

chief_complaint.value: my left ear is blocked up

clinical_assessment.assessment: a plug of wax pressing on the eardrum

clinical_actions.description: Arrange ear syringing by the nurse
Avoid cotton buds and keep water out of the ear
